title: "4.2 Data and sample"
order: 2
---

## Source

One file, `shared/data/raw/businesses.parquet`: {{< var score.n_applicants >}} applicants,
one row each, drawn by the platform's data generator ([D2](../d2-data.qmd)). The target is
`default`. The generator gives every applicant an outcome, booked or not, which a real
bank's data never would; that is what lets this chapter measure the model on both
populations below.

## Features

The model uses the {{< var score.n_features >}} columns of `FEATURE_COLUMNS`
(`score/src/feature_engineering.py`): twelve read directly from the data and three ratios
built from it by `compute_features`.

| Kind | Columns |
|---|---|
| Firmographic | `years_in_business`, `annual_revenue`, `industry`, `entity_type` |
| Financial statement | `dscr`, `current_ratio`, `leverage` |
| Bureau (credit file) | `utilization`, `credit_history_months`, `prior_delinquencies`, `trade_lines` |
| Public record | `public_records` |
| Derived ratios | `debt_to_income` (total debt over net income), `revenue_per_employee`, `profit_margin` (net income over revenue) |

`industry` and `entity_type` are categorical; the other {{< var score.n_numeric >}} are
numeric. `compute_features` turns any missing or non-numeric value in a numeric column
into zero. The generated data contain none, so on this data the rule changes nothing; on
data with gaps it would score a missing value as zero without warning, which is recorded
as an observation in [4.7](limitations.qmd#observations).

## Split and seed

The split is drawn once, in `score/src/train.py`, and redrawn identically by `verify.py`
and by the facts behind this chapter:

```python
SEED = 42    # shared/config.py
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED, stratify=y)
```

That gives {{< var score.n_train >}} training rows and {{< var score.n_test >}} held-out
rows (the held-out {{< var score.test_share >}}), stratified on `default` so both carry
the same default rate, to within one row. Every "held-out" metric in this chapter is
measured on those {{< var score.n_test >}} rows, which the scorecard never saw while it was
fitted. The adjudication model splits the same rows with the same seed and the same
stratification, so its held-out applicants are the same ones
([4.5](performance.qmd#benchmark)).

## Two populations

The model **trains and gates on applicants, while the bank lends to the
{{< var score.n_booked >}} it books.** Within the held-out split:

{{< include ../../_generated/score-populations.md >}}

The gate ([4.9](gate.qmd)) is measured on the first row. The booked applicants are the
population every loan decision after origination is made on, and there the same model
ranks noticeably worse. Why that is so, and what is done about it, are finding 2 in
[4.7](limitations.qmd).

## Leakage controls

The platform keeps one deny-list of columns that do not exist when the decision is made
([D2](../d2-data.qmd#leakage-controls) gives the list and its three enforcement points):

```python
LEAKAGE_COLUMNS = [                   # shared/config.py
    "pd_default_origination",     # DGP ground-truth PD
    "default",                    # scorecard/adjudication target
    "risk_based_rate",            # priced from the true PD
    "booked",                     # funding decision (post-adjudication)
    "deterioration_next_6_12mo",  # downstream early-warning target
    "line_increase_good",         # downstream line-increase target
]
```

For the scorecard the control is its fixed feature list, checked by the test suite:

```python
def test_score_features_are_leakage_free():      # tests/test_leakage.py
    assert set(FEATURE_COLUMNS).isdisjoint(LEAKAGE_COLUMNS)
```

`score/src/train.py` itself does not assert against the deny-list, unlike the downstream
trainers; the list it trains on is a constant, and the test fails the suite if a denied
column is ever added to it.

## Exclusions

None. Every applicant is in either the training or the held-out split.
